saml.description: When SAML username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor falls back to email, then to NameID, to populate the username.
saml.note: Identity names differing from the sent NameID may be expected if email is present and used as the username.

saml.description: Casdoor normalizes email addresses to lowercase for uniqueness and duplicate checking.
saml.note: Case-only differences in email should not be treated as distinct principals.

saml.description: Soft-deleted users cannot sign in through any authentication method, including third-party login.
saml.note: Rejected login for a previously linked identity may be due to soft deletion, not broken federation.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and require explicit user selection, even when only one SAML provider is configured.
saml.note: Lack of automatic redirect is by design and should not be treated as flow inconsistency.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login for the same user and application terminates previous sessions.
saml.note: A prior session becoming invalid after a second login is expected behavior, not replay protection or session corruption.

saml.description: Calling /api/sso-logout without logoutAll=false logs the user out from all sessions and expires all tokens.
saml.note: Unexpected loss of other sessions after logout is by design unless session-only logout was explicitly requested.

saml.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the token's granted scopes.
saml.note: Missing email/profile fields in userinfo are expected when those scopes were not requested.

saml.description: Shared applications use organization-specific client identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName>.
saml.note: Different effective client IDs for the same shared app across orgs are expected and should not be treated as audience confusion.

saml.description: Casdoor can be configured to sign only the SAML response envelope and not the assertion itself.
saml.note: Acceptance of response-only signatures may reflect compatibility configuration rather than insecure parsing.

saml.constraint: Casdoor as SAML SP uses /api/acs and the documentation states it accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST treat SAML responses as HTTP POST binding submissions; GET-based ACS tests are invalid setup and any rejection is not a security finding.

saml.constraint: Casdoor SAML login is SP-initiated from the login page and SAML providers always display a button that the user must click. The fuzzer MUST model a browser authorization/login initiation step before any SAML assertion delivery; sending a bare unsolicited assertion to Casdoor without initiating the flow can fail for flow reasons rather than security checks.

Casdoor extracts the username from SAML assertions using a fallback chain: configured username mapping, else email, else NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID because different upstream identities can intentionally collapse if username mapping is absent and both resolve to the same fallback value.

For SAML email-binding collision and account-linking tests, Casdoor may derive the local username from email when username mapping is absent. The fuzzer MUST distinguish username derivation from account-linking bugs: a collision caused by identical fallback email/NameID values is by-design mapping behavior unless different upstream values unexpectedly resolve to the same downstream account.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking by email/phone or case-insensitive username for external providers. For I4 tests involving SAML identities, the fuzzer MUST account for by-design linking behavior when an incoming SAML identity matches an existing local account on enabled linking attributes; otherwise identity merges may be false positives.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo response is scope-dependent. The fuzzer MUST request the needed scopes during authorization/token issuance before using verify_granted_identity to compare fields like email or profile attributes; missing fields due to omitted scopes are not identity-binding failures.

When testing audience binding on downstream OAuth tokens after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If the authorization request includes resource, the token request MUST include the exact same resource value; otherwise audience-related failures may be caused by request mismatch rather than proper audience enforcement.

Application token lifetime parameters have sentinel semantics: RefreshExpireInHours default is 0 hours, and Code resend timeout set to 0 means use the global default rather than literal zero. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret 0 as 'disabled' or immediate expiry without checking field semantics.

For I2 freshness tests against OAuth tokens issued after SAML login, the sequence MUST include a control login with a valid token/session because failures can also result from application settings such as DisableSignin, failed sign-in lockout, exclusive sign-in, or missing provider attachment rather than token freshness enforcement.

Exclusive sign-in is a documented application feature: a new sign-in deletes prior sessions for that user and application. For replay/coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST disable or account for EnableExclusiveSignin, otherwise a second login invalidating the first session is by design and can masquerade as replay protection or session confusion.

SSO logout supports logoutAll=true by default and logoutAll=false for current-session-only. The fuzzer MUST choose the intended mode explicitly during cleanup and session tests; omitting logoutAll triggers full logout across applications and can invalidate unrelated sessions, corrupting multi-step coherence tests.

Casdoor's token introspection endpoint is protected by HTTP Basic authentication using client_id:client_secret, not bearer token auth. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection with client credentials or introspection failures will be setup errors, not token invalidity.

For SAML assertion signature tests, Casdoor documentation describes provider-side parsing of IdP metadata into Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL. The fuzzer MUST configure the provider with explicit trusted metadata/issuer before testing forged assertions; otherwise acceptance/rejection may reflect incomplete provider setup rather than signature or issuer validation behavior.

Casdoor's SAML SP docs do not document any wildcard or regex matching mode for SAML username/email attribute mapping. The fuzzer MUST assume exact attribute-name mapping only; for multi-identity I4 scenarios, do not rely on wildcard attribute names to match multiple upstream fields.

Shared applications intentionally rewrite the effective client_id/application reference by appending -org-<organization>. For cross-org audience or identity-isolation tests, the fuzzer MUST treat org-suffixed client IDs as distinct relying parties; cross-org acceptance may be expected if the same shared application is intentionally reused.

Application tags intentionally restrict sign-in to users whose tags intersect the application's tags, except admins/global admins. The fuzzer MUST align user tags with application tags in authorization-binding tests; login denial from tag mismatch is expected policy behavior, not an authn bug.

Casdoor supports account linking via email and case-insensitive username. For case-confusion I4 tests, the fuzzer MUST know that case-insensitive username linking can intentionally merge identities; only unexpected merges outside documented linking rules should be flagged.

Casdoor as SAML SP uses a single ACS endpoint at /api/acs and the documentation states it accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST send SAMLResponse via HTTP POST form submission to /api/acs; GET-based callbacks are invalid for Casdoor-as-SP tests.

For SAML provider setup, Casdoor expects IdP metadata to be pasted into the provider's metadata field and then parsed to populate endpoint, IdP, issuerUrl, SP ACS URL, and SP Entity ID. The fuzzer MUST supply valid metadata when creating the provider; manually omitting metadata risks an unconfigured trust anchor and invalid test results.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature-validation tests, Casdoor documentation only describes trust establishment from configured IdP metadata/certificate. The fuzzer MUST create the SAML provider with explicit metadata and then submit forged assertions to /api/acs; do NOT treat missing provider metadata as a meaningful insecure default because the docs do not state that Casdoor trusts certificates from the response itself.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, Casdoor provider configuration derives issuerUrl/IdP from parsed metadata. The fuzzer MUST configure a provider with known metadata first, then mutate the assertion Issuer to a different value. Without a configured provider issuer baseline, issuer-mismatch results are uninterpretable.

For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion and saml_spurious_signature, Casdoor documentation distinguishes response-envelope signing from assertion signing on the IdP side and notes assertion signatures are optional for compatibility when Casdoor acts as IdP. Therefore, when Casdoor acts as SP, the fuzzer MUST test whether /api/acs accepts a response signed only at the envelope level versus assertion level separately; acceptance of envelope-only signatures may be by-design interoperability depending on SP validation behavior and must be interpreted carefully.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, the fuzzer MUST include a control login with a valid SAML assertion before sending an expired assertion. Otherwise, a failed expired-assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

For I2 replay tests against SAML assertions (assertion ID replay or OneTimeUse), the fuzzer MUST reuse the same provider and application configuration across both submissions. Recreating the provider or changing application settings between submissions would invalidate replay conclusions.

Casdoor's SAML SP login is initiated from the login page by clicking a provider button; SAML providers do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. The fuzzer MUST explicitly initiate the SAML flow before posting the forged SAMLResponse so that RelayState/InResponseTo context exists.

Casdoor's SAML user mapping falls back from configured username mapping to email, then to NameID when username is absent. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this fallback chain: if username mapping is missing or empty, identities may intentionally bind by email first and then NameID. To isolate NameID-based behavior, omit email; to test email-binding collision, provide conflicting email explicitly.

Casdoor supports account linking by email and documents automatic account linking for external providers, plus application setting enableLinkWithEmail. For I4 unverified_email_account_linking and saml_email_binding_collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control application/provider linking settings and compare resulting user identity carefully; account merges by email may be configured behavior rather than a protocol parsing flaw.

For I4 cross-org and shared-application tests, shared applications use an org-specific suffix '-org-<organizationName>' on client_id/application name. The fuzzer MUST use the organization-specific client_id when targeting a shared application; otherwise, cross-organization identity results may reflect wrong application routing rather than an identity-binding flaw.
Numeric sentinel: application CodeResendTimeout uses 0 as 'use global default' rather than literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown instead.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as 'use default' rather than literal zero lifetime. The documented default is 720 hours, and sessions without Remember Me are limited to 24 hours. Never use 0 expecting immediate expiry.

Numeric sentinel: application RefreshExpireInHours defaults to 0 hours in the docs for refresh-token configuration. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as effectively disabling refresh-token lifetime/availability rather than a usable long-lived refresh token, and should set an explicit positive value when refresh behavior is under test.

Session-use budget: Casdoor supports exclusive sign-in, which invalidates prior sessions on each new login for the same user/application. In multi-login sequences, the fuzzer MUST NOT expect earlier session tokens to remain valid after a later login when EnableExclusiveSignin is enabled.

For I3 config-change sequences, Casdoor application/provider changes are expected to affect NEW logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests before and after config change, not treat an admin-driven configuration update itself as a vulnerability.

For I5 audience/resource binding, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators and requires the resource parameter to match exactly between authorization and token requests. The fuzzer MUST send the same resource value in both start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token when testing audience-bound access tokens.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, Casdoor documentation states omitted scope inherits the subject token scope and specified scope should be a subset of the original. The fuzzer MUST include a baseline subject token with known limited scope and then request an expanded scope during token exchange to detect improper broadening.

For I2 freshness tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML login, include a control token request using a valid code/token flow. Without a control, failures may stem from broken application grant-type configuration rather than freshness enforcement.

Casdoor is multi-tenant and resources carry owner/organization fields. The fuzzer MUST keep owner semantics consistent across resource types: users belong to an organization owner, while applications/providers may be created under the admin or organization owner as configured. Using the wrong owner value can make providers invisible to applications or users inaccessible to tests.
Casdoor SAML ACS is POST-only at /api/acs. The fuzzer MUST send SAMLResponse via HTTP POST form submission; GET-based ACS tests are invalid setup and will fail regardless of SAML security behavior.

For SAML login tests, Casdoor acts as SP and requires the external IdP to be configured with ACS URL = Entity ID = https://<casdoor-domain>/api/acs. The fuzzer MUST keep these values aligned when creating SAML providers; mismatched SP Entity ID / ACS URL causes setup failure unrelated to invariant violations.

Casdoor SAML provider creation is metadata-driven. The fuzzer SHOULD provide IdP metadata in provider.metadata and rely on Parse-generated endpoint/idP/issuerUrl values rather than inventing partial manual settings; otherwise issuer/endpoint trust may be misconfigured and produce false I1 results.

When testing signed AuthnRequest behavior, Casdoor only signs requests if provider.enableSignAuthnRequest is enabled. Do NOT interpret unsigned AuthnRequest behavior as a proof-integrity bug unless this setting was intentionally enabled for the test.

Casdoor supports a username fallback chain for SAML user creation/linking: configured username mapping, else email, else NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID because omitting username mapping can legitimately cause identities to bind by email or NameID.

For saml_email_binding_collision and unverified-email-style identity tests, Casdoor may use email as the username fallback when username mapping is absent. The fuzzer MUST create control cases with distinct email and NameID values and MUST NOT assume NameID is always the binding key.

Casdoor can auto-link external logins by email when application.enableLinkWithEmail is enabled. For I4 account-linking tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set this application flag to the intended state; otherwise email-based merges may be by design rather than a vulnerability.

SAML providers always appear as explicit buttons on the login page and do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. Tests that expect automatic redirect into SAML are invalid; the flow must explicitly initiate the SAML provider selection first.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, include a control login with a valid assertion first. Casdoor docs only state ACS POST handling and provider setup; without a control, a failed expired-assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application configuration.

Application.expireInHours and refreshExpireInHours are token lifetime controls. Numeric sentinel: refreshExpireInHours value 0 means default 0 hours per docs, not an implicit nonzero default. Do not assume 0 disables expiry checks or grants long-lived refresh tokens.

Application.codeResendTimeout uses sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the global default, while positive values are literal seconds. Never assume 0 means immediate resend; tests involving repeated verification-code requests must account for inherited default throttling.

Application.cookieExpireInHours uses sentinel semantics: 0 means use the default cookie lifetime, not zero-hour expiry. Also, without 'Remember me', session lifetime is limited to 24 hours by design. Do not treat shorter cookie lifetime as freshness enforcement failure.

Exclusive sign-in is per application: a new sign-in deletes prior sessions for that user and application. For replay/coherence tests using multiple concurrent sessions, the fuzzer MUST disable enableExclusiveSignin unless the test specifically targets session replacement behavior.

For I3 config-change tests, Casdoor application/provider updates legitimately affect subsequent logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same logical flow before and after config change, not treat expected post-update behavior as a bug.

Casdoor supports disabling SAML assertion signatures while keeping the response envelope signed via application.enableSamlAssertionSignature=false. For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion / spurious-signature tests, the fuzzer MUST record this setting: acceptance of response-only signatures may be configured compatibility behavior, not necessarily insecure default.

Casdoor can disable SAML attributes entirely via application.disableSamlAttributes. For I4/I5 tests that rely on email, displayName, roles, or other attributes being present in the assertion, the fuzzer MUST ensure this flag is false; otherwise missing attributes are by design.

If application.useEmailAsSamlNameId is enabled, Casdoor as IdP emits email as NameID instead of username. For cross-protocol and collision tests involving downstream SP identity, the fuzzer MUST account for this alternate principal representation and not assume NameID equals username.

Casdoor OAuth token exchange inherits the subject token scope when scope is omitted, and allows requesting a subset when scope is provided. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST compare requested scope against original scope and treat omitted-scope inheritance as by design, not escalation.

When using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. For audience-binding tests, mismatched resource values cause setup failure and must not be misread as audience enforcement.

Token introspection at /api/login/oauth/introspect requires HTTP Basic authentication with client_id:client_secret. The fuzzer MUST authenticate as the client, not with the bearer token itself, or introspection failures will be false positives.

Casdoor userinfo returns claims according to granted scope. For I4/I5 verification, the fuzzer MUST request the needed scopes during login; absent email/profile claims in /api/userinfo are by design when scope is limited.

Applications and providers are organization-scoped resources. The fuzzer MUST keep owner/organization relationships consistent when creating users, applications, and SAML providers, or provider visibility/attachment may fail for tenancy reasons unrelated to security invariants.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise.
